Order service API

All responses are JSON unless noted. Requests are made to the address this service is running on.

GET /docs
    This page (plain text).

GET /value
    Returns {"value": <integer>}. No authentication.

POST /token
    Returns {"token": "<token>"}. No authentication. Send the token on authenticated
    requests in the header "Authorization: Bearer <token>".

GET /orders?page=N
    Authenticated. Lists orders, 50 per page; N starts at 1.
    Returns {"page", "total_pages", "items", "next"}. "next" is the path of the following
    page, or null on the last page.
    Each order has: id, customer_id, status, placed_at, amount_cents.
    status is one of: placed, shipped, cancelled, returned.
    placed_at is an ISO 8601 timestamp. amount_cents is an integer number of cents.

GET /customers/{id}
    Authenticated. Returns {"id", "name", "region", "tier", "discount_pct"}; 404 if the id is unknown.
    region is one of: north, south, east, west. discount_pct is a whole-number percentage.

The shipped-orders total for 1 March to 31 May 2025 (UTC), after customer discounts, is **9,329,707 cents**. That covers **407** distinct qualifying orders, and `result.json` is written in the workspace root.

|---|---|
| north | 2,666,579 |
| south | 2,714,624 |
| east | 1,671,579 |
| west | 2,276,925 |

- **Duplicates:** I discarded 20 repeated listings. The service returned 1,500 rows over 30 pages, which is 1,480 distinct orders plus those 20 repeats, so nothing was missed.

- **Surprises:** None in the data. The service did not fail or refuse any request during the run, so I never hit the rate limit or a token expiry. My script would have waited and retried on a rate limit and fetched a new token on expiry.

- **Scripts:** The working script is in `/tmp/work`, outside the workspace.
